title: Third Conditional
subtitle: Talk about unreal situations in the past — things that didn't happen.
objectives: Form the third conditional for unreal past situations (things that didn't happen)
Tell the second and third conditionals apart based on time

content.intro: You already know the second conditional for imaginary situations now. The third conditional imagines a different past: what would have happened if things had been different.

rules.heading: Third conditional — unreal past
rules.body:
If + past perfect, would have + past participle. Used for something that didn't actually happen in the past.

  • If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam. (I didn't study harder, so I didn't pass)
  • If she had left earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.

examples: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If she had left earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.
If they had known, they would have helped.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I had study harder, I would have passed.
commonMistakes.right: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.
commonMistakes.why: The third conditional's "if" clause needs the past perfect (had + past participle).

commonMistakes.wrong: If I had studied harder, I would passed the exam.
commonMistakes.right: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
commonMistakes.why: The result clause of the third conditional needs "would have" + past participle.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks (Part 1 of 3)
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct second or third conditional form.

items.prompt: If I ___ (study) harder, I ___ (pass) the exam. (but I didn't study)
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If she ___ (leave) earlier, she ___ (not/miss) the train.
items.explanation: Third conditional, unreal past.

items.prompt: If they ___ (leave) earlier, they ___ (not/miss) the flight.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If he ___ (be) more careful, he ___ (not/break) the vase.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If we ___ (check) the weather, we ___ (not/get) soaked.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes something that didn't actually happen in the past?
options: If it rains, I will stay home.
If I had known, I would have called you.
If I won the lottery, I would travel.
items.explanation: This is the third conditional — an unreal past situation.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a third conditional?
options: If it rains, I'll stay in.
If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.
If I were rich, I would travel.
items.explanation: An unreal past situation — third conditional.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly forms the third conditional result?
options: I would help if I had known.
I would have helped if I had known.
I would have help if I had known.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result needs "would have" + past participle.

items.prompt: How do you ask about an unreal past situation?
options: What would you have done if you had known?
What would you do if you had known?
What did you do if you knew?
items.explanation: A third-conditional question uses would have + past participle in the result clause.

items.incorrect: If they had known, they would help.
answer: If they had known, they would have helped.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result clause needs "would have" + past participle.

items.incorrect: If she had studied, she would pass.
answer: If she had studied, she would have passed.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result clause needs "would have" + past participle.

items.incorrect: If I would have known, I would have called.
answer: If I had known, I would have called.
items.explanation: The "if" clause of the third conditional never uses "would" — use the past perfect.

items.incorrect: If you had known, you would have called?
answer: If you had known, would you have called?
If you had known, would you have called
items.explanation: A question inverts "would" and the subject in the result clause: would you have called?

items.incorrect: If he had left earlier, he would arrive on time.
answer: If he had left earlier, he would have arrived on time.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result clause needs "would have" + past participle.

items.incorrect: If they would have known, they would have come.
answer: If they had known, they would have come.
items.explanation: The "if" clause of the third conditional never uses "would" — use the past perfect.

items.incorrect: If you study harder, you would have passed.
answer: If you had studied harder, you would have passed.
items.explanation: Mixing a present if-clause with a third-conditional result doesn't work — the if-clause also needs the past perfect.

items.incorrect: If I had known, I would called you.
answer: If I had known, I would have called you.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result clause needs "would have" + past participle, not "would" + base verb.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks (Part 2 of 3)
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct second or third conditional form.

items.prompt: If she ___ (know) about the meeting, she ___ (come).
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If you ___ (ask) me, I ___ (help) you.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (check) the map, I ___ (not/get) lost.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If she ___ (arrive) on time, she ___ (not/miss) the flight.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: If he ___ (not/lose) his phone, he ___ (call) us.
items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes an unreal past situation?
options: If I study, I will pass.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I study, I would pass.
items.explanation: This is the third conditional — an unreal past situation.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly completes a third conditional?
options: If we had left earlier, we would arrive on time.
If we had left earlier, we would have arrived on time.
If we left earlier, we would have arrived on time.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result clause needs "would have" + past participle.

items.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: If she had known, she would have told us.
If she knew, she would have told us.
If she had known, she would tell us.
items.explanation: A consistent third conditional needs a past-perfect if-clause and a "would have" result clause together.

items.prompt: Which if-clause verb form is correct for the third conditional?
options: If I would have seen you...
If I had seen you...
If I saw you...
items.explanation: The if-clause of the third conditional never uses "would" — it needs the past perfect.

items.prompt: How do you ask what someone would have done in an unreal past situation?
options: What would you have done if you had missed the flight?
What would you do if you missed the flight?
What did you do if you had missed the flight?
items.explanation: A third-conditional question uses "would have" + past participle in the result clause.

items.explanation: Unreal past — third conditional.

summary: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle — unreal past (didn't happen).
Compare: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb — unreal present/future.
